A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CamSAM2, with matching architecture, equations and core experiments. Text, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v3 includes a readable appendix and conference checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original CamSAM2 evaluations on MoCA-Mask, CAD and SUN-SEG, qualitative comparisons and component ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds baseline comparisons, sensitivity experiments, ablations, runtime measurements and qualitative analyses in its appendix.

M1.justification: The decamouflaged token, IOF, EOF, FPS plus one-iteration k-means in OPG, BCE/Dice objective and logit-averaging inference remain unchanged. Appendix explanations, including bypassing the added modules to recover SAM2, do not establish a revised VCOS algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use MoCA-Mask/MoCA-Mask-Pseudo, CAD and SUN-SEG-Easy/Hard for the same animal and polyp segmentation tasks. Additional experiments vary backbones, click budgets or evaluated frame subsets within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds SAM2-FT, with its mask decoder fine-tuned, to all three prompt settings in Table 1. Appendix A.4/Table 10 additionally evaluates retrained SAM2-Adapter, previously only cited. These introduce important adaptation-specific controls; A.4 acknowledges that SAM2-Adapter uses different temporal and prompt settings.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported training budget from 15 to 10 epochs, without establishing whether existing experiments were rerun. New protocols evaluate Hiera-B+/L, 2/3/5-click budgets, first-frame-only segmentation and runtime/FLOPs, including latency on a 106-frame video. Dataset splits and the seven segmentation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original component, distance-metric and prototype-count ablations remain. v3 adds tests of logit averaging, first-frame performance, token count, sampling/clustering choices and click sensitivity, plus efficiency profiling, prototype-similarity maps and further qualitative cases (A.3, A.5-A.8 and A.11-A.12). These substantially expand investigation of design choices and behavior.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 newly specifies random seed 42 for sampling click prompts; v1 gives no seed. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v3 explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical significance reporting in its checklist.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for new comparisons, sensitivity tests, ablations and computational costs. Table 2 also revises existing Hiera-S entries: CamSAM2 box-prompt mDice/mIoU changes from 75.5/65.4 to 76.4/66.1. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting gains given the changed training-budget description. Original Hiera-T, CAD, SUN-SEG and Tables 5-7 values are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(7), defining feature fusion, prototype generation and the training objective, are unchanged. Neither version provides theoretical results or proofs. The added mechanism discussions and empirical analyses introduce no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: adapting frozen SAM2 through the token and three modules, improving VCOS with minimal prompts, transferring to CAD and preserving access to SAM2's original capabilities. Additional evidence and revised numerical gains do not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains why token interactions change SAM2 outputs despite frozen parameters and why disabling the additions restores original behavior (A.5 and A.9). It also discusses SAM2-Adapter comparison fairness, prototype behavior and explicit limitations involving shot changes and long occlusions (A.4, A.10-A.11), substantially extending v1's interpretation and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly documents eight-frame clips, 1024x1024 inputs, 256x256 targets, batch size four and mask resizing for memory encoding. v3 reports code availability rather than a future release. Conversely, v1's StepLR specification disappears; this is lost documentation, not evidence that the scheduler was removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds HQ-SAM as inspiration for the existing averaging strategy and explains its distinction from earlier SAM2 studies and SAM2-Adapter more explicitly (Section 2.3 and A.4-A.5). Most cited works and the broader positioning are retained; publication and bibliographic updates do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The main narrative and much of the prose remain closely matched. v3 tightens explanatory and results paragraphs, moves training/inference from Section 3.6 into Section 4.1, updates author information and adds acknowledgments, appendix subsections and a checklist. Existing prose is locally revised rather than comprehensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column conference format, redraws Figure 1 and restructures Table 2 with backbones in adjacent columns. It also adds Tables 8-16 and Figures 5-9. These include new analyses and illustrations alongside redisplayed results, constituting substantial visual and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The fine-tuned SAM2 control addresses an important gap in v1's evidence for architectural benefits beyond task adaptation. New averaging, prototype and first-frame analyses, measured overhead, reproducibility details and explicit failure conditions substantially strengthen validation and transparency. The unexplained epoch revision, omitted scheduler detail and absent uncertainty estimates remain weaknesses, and the SAM2-Adapter comparison has unequal inputs. Nevertheless, the added controls and explanations provide a clear substantial net improvement.
